title: p_c refinement diagnostic — does refined p_c resolve exponent deviations?
note: FROZEN before any execution. Motivation: Q-P006 measured D_f=1.863+0.042, Gn=1.730+0.060, Bn=0.137+0.041, Tau=1.975+0.005 at L in {512,1024,2048}. Tau fails at 16.6 sigma vs Fisher value 187/91=2.055. Two hypotheses: (H1) p_c is slightly inaccurate, causing systematic bias in all exponents; (H2) finite-size effects bias tau estimation. This experiment tests H1 by measuring p_c via width-curve crossing at L in {512,1024,2048} and comparing to Ziff's value 0.59274605079210. Also re-measures tau at refined p_c to check convergence. Uses same G_LAB rng(EXP-0004-certified). No cells from EXP-0009/EXP-0010/Q-P006 reused.

p_c_width.note: width-curve crossing at L in {512,1024,2048}; L->inf extrapolation

tau_at_refined_pc.note: if H1 (p_c accuracy) explains tau deviation, refined p_c should bring tau closer to Fisher value

gates.C7: pure-Python union-find independent: L in {512,1024}, subsample n=30
gates.FG: slope stability of D_f on inner L values

decision_rule.H0_SUPPORTED: all gates PASS, p_c within 0.001 of Ziff, tau improved at refined p_c
decision_rule.ABNORMAL: gates PASS, some metrics out of tolerance but H1 or H2 supported
